h2: Magnetic particle inspection in Illinois: where the work is and how state rules shape it
html:
Magnetic particle inspection in Illinois: where the work is and how state rules shape it

Magnetic particle inspection in Illinois is mostly crack detection on ferromagnetic steel: repair and attachment welds on registered boilers and vessels, gears and forgings from Rockford-area manufacturers, and mill equipment on the lake shore just across the Indiana line. Atlantis mobilises MT crews from Houston, examines to ASME Section V Article 7 or ASTM E1444 as the contract requires, and prepares a separate quote for every scope.

Repairs on registered equipment. Illinois rules require licensed repair organisations to file National Board Form R-1 after a repair and Form R-2 after an alteration. Owner-users that hold a National Board R-Certificate or an Illinois repair firm certificate and work on their own equipment keep those forms on file rather than submitting them. MT on the excavation and on the completed weld is part of the evidence behind that form, with acceptance taken from the construction code. Used or relocated equipment also needs a certificate inspection before it runs again, which often brings surface examination of nozzles, lugs and supports into scope.

Rockford manufacturing. The Rockford area counts more than 70 aerospace supply-chain companies employing around 7,000 people. Woodward builds jet engine fuel systems at its Loves Park plant, and Forest City Gear in Roscoe has made gears for NASA's Mars rovers. Gear and shaft producers rely on wet fluorescent MT to find grinding and heat-treatment cracks. Aerospace parts follow ASTM E1444 and the customer's specification with personnel certified under written practices aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Steel on the lake shore. Indiana has been the top steel-producing state since at least 1980, according to the American Iron and Steel Institute, and Cleveland-Cliffs bought ArcelorMittal's US mills, Indiana Harbor among them, in 2020. Indiana Harbor in East Chicago runs one blast furnace, No. 7, alongside four basic oxygen furnaces. Ladle trunnions, crane hooks, couplings and roll necks are examined with MT on maintenance and statutory cycles. Equipment on the Indiana side answers to the Indiana Department of Homeland Security's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety program, not to Illinois.

Coatings and access. Much of the in-service steel in Illinois plants and mills is painted. Article 7 permits examination through a thin non-magnetic coating only up to a stated limit, and anything thicker needs either a demonstration on a coated reference piece or removal back to metal. Agreeing which applies before the crew arrives avoids a day lost to blasting, and it decides whether the owner's coating contractor needs to be scheduled ahead of the MT technicians.

Technique choices that come up on Illinois MT scopes:

  • AC yokes for field welds, with the lift check Article 7 requires before use; prods are kept off finished pressure-retaining surfaces because an arc strike is itself a rejectable condition.
  • Wet fluorescent particles where sensitivity matters, which brings a darkened viewing area and UV-A intensity checks.
  • Inside Chicago, the Department of Buildings Boiler Inspection Bureau is the jurisdiction, so the city's requirements for repair records are confirmed before work starts.

The national magnetic particle testing service sets out what each examination includes, weld inspection in Chicago covers fabrication and repair welds, and NDT inspection services in Illinois maps the rest of the state. For MT training and certification, start with the magnetic particle testing course and the MT simulator. To discuss an Illinois MT scope, send the details.
